threads.thread_goal: Align on membership tier structure, pricing, and policy constraints.

messages.text: Kicking off the membership structure work for our new program. I have a first rough draft for T1 captured in the Tiered Membership Structure and Pricing doc A1. It outlines three tiers for launch: Basic, Plus, and Premium, with increasing benefits and price points. I also started a skeleton for the Membership Policy and Internal FAQ A5 so we can plug in constraints as we go and then complete T2. Before I go deeper, I would like your feedback on whether three tiers feels manageable for the sales conversations and if any obvious policy red flags come to mind.

Thanks for sharing A1. Three tiers sounds workable as long as the differences are very clear in one glance. For T1, can you summarize the core benefit jump from Basic to Plus and Plus to Premium here in the thread? That will help us see if anything feels redundant or too complex. On the policy side, I will rely on you and legal, but from a sales angle we should avoid any benefit that is hard to explain in under 10 seconds.

Agree that three tiers is fine if we keep the story simple. From past launches, confusion usually comes from edge cases like upgrades and downgrades. When you expand A5 for T2, can you make sure we have a very clear rule on when someone can move between tiers and how proration works, even if we are not changing the billing system? That will avoid awkward calls later.

I went through A1 quickly. I like that Premium has the most benefits, but I am not fully sure how to explain the difference between Basic and Plus yet. Maybe we can have a short one line description for each tier that we can reuse later in the script for T3. Also, could we add a simple example in A5 about a customer upgrading mid month so I can see how we should talk about it on the phone.

Three tiers feels like the right balance. From a targeting point of view for T4 later, I would map Basic to price sensitive leads, Plus to those asking for a bit more flexibility, and Premium to our most engaged accounts. For pricing, do we already have guidance from finance on the bands, or should we propose ranges in A1 and then send for validation as part of T2?

Here is a quick summary of the draft in A1 for T1: Basic focuses on access to core services only. Plus adds priority support and a small bundle of extra services. Premium adds all Plus benefits plus exclusive perks and the highest support level. I will add one line descriptions for each tier in A1 and mirror them in A5 so we keep the wording consistent. For pricing, I have an initial range based on our current offers but I have not yet checked with finance or legal, so we should treat it as a proposal until T2 is complete.

That breakdown helps. From a sales conversation, I would suggest we anchor Plus as the default recommendation and use Basic only when someone clearly pushes back on price. Premium can be positioned as the best value for heavy users. For T1, can we make sure the benefits ladder is visible in a simple table in A1 so reps can see what is added at each step without reading long text?

Good point on upgrades and downgrades. For T2 I will add a dedicated section in A5 covering eligibility, upgrade and downgrade rules, and cancellations, with a couple of concrete examples including mid cycle changes. I will also flag any parts that need explicit legal or finance review before we call it final.

On the pricing bands, I would recommend we keep round numbers that are easy to say on a call and easy to show on a slide. If we end up with too many decimals, it slows down the pitch. Maybe we can define a target price and a small discount window in A1, and then you validate with finance as part of T2 so we know what we can offer without extra approvals.

The table idea in A1 would help me a lot. Sometimes I mix up which benefit belongs to which tier when there are many bullet points. If we can also highlight in A5 which benefits are non negotiable, that will make it easier to avoid promising something that is not allowed.

For discounts, I suggest we keep it simple for launch: a standard introductory discount for the first term and maybe a small incentive for annual commitments. Anything more complex will be hard to track in A4 later. We can document the allowed discount rules in A5 during T2 so everyone knows the boundaries.

I have updated A1 with the tier table and one line descriptions, and I added a draft section in A5 for discount rules, including a standard introductory discount and an annual commitment incentive as you suggested. I will now send both A1 and A5 to finance and legal for a quick review as part of T2. Once they confirm, we can lock the pricing bands and discount rules for launch.

Once finance and legal sign off, I am comfortable saying we go live with three tiers. From a sales standpoint, the benefits ladder and the discount rules you described are clear enough for us to build the script T3 and objection handling T7 on top of them.

Finance and legal have now reviewed A1 and A5 and confirmed that the three tier structure, pricing bands, and the two standard discount rules are aligned with our current policies and consumer protection requirements. Unless there are strong objections, I propose we formally confirm three tiers for launch with the benefits as described in A1.

No objections from me. The three tiers in A1 are clear, and the discount rules in A5 are simple enough to explain. This gives us a solid base to start preparing the pitch and the pilot calls later on.

Aligned here as well. Three tiers with the current benefits and the approved pricing and discount rules work for the outreach plan we will build in T4 and T5. I will start thinking about which segments map best to each tier.
Works for me too. With the table in A1 and the examples in A5, I feel more confident explaining the differences between the tiers and the basic discount rules on calls.

Great, I will mark in A1 and A5 that we are going ahead with three tiers and the confirmed pricing bands and discount rules for launch. I will also note in A5 that any exceptions beyond these rules need manager approval so we stay within policy.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize sales script, objection handling, and pre-call checklist.

messages.text: I have drafted the Membership Sales Script and Call Outline A2 and the Objection Handling Cheat Sheet A3 for T3 and T7, based on the three tiers we just aligned in A1. The script follows a simple flow: open, discovery, tier recommendation, handle objections, and close. The cheat sheet currently covers ten common objections. I also started a Pre Call Membership Pitch Preparation Checklist A7 so we do not forget key steps before dialing. Please review and comment, especially on anything that feels too long or hard to say naturally.

I went through A2. The flow feels natural, but the discovery section might be a bit long for shorter calls. Maybe we can trim a couple of questions and keep only the ones that really help us decide between Basic, Plus, and Premium. In A3, I like that you grouped objections by theme. Could we add one more around confusion between tiers, since that will probably come up early on?

I read A2 and A3 as well. The structure helps me, but I am not sure how to adapt the script when a customer jumps straight to asking about price. Could we add a short alternative path in A2 for that situation? Also, in A7, maybe we can include a reminder to check A5 for any special policy notes before the call.

Nice work on A2 and A3. For T3, I suggest we tighten the close section with a clear default ask, like suggesting Plus unless the discovery clearly points to Basic or Premium. On A7, we might want to add a quick check that the prospect is correctly tagged in A4 so we can track which tier we pitched and the outcome.

From a membership and policy angle, A2 and A3 look generally aligned with A1 and A5. I will add a couple of notes in A2 where we need to be careful with wording around guarantees and cancellation terms so we stay within what we documented in A5. Once we finalize the content, I will mark T3 and T7 as ready from my side.

Good call on the discovery length. I will cut it down to three core questions in A2 that map directly to tier choice and remove the rest. I will also add an objection in A3 for confusion between tiers, with a short explanation that references the simple ladder from A1. That should help keep the conversation focused.

On the price first scenario, I will add a short branch in A2: acknowledge the price question, give a quick range, then move back to one or two discovery questions before recommending a tier. I will also update A7 to include a reminder to skim A5 for any special notes on that segment or region before the call.

I like the idea of three core discovery questions. That will make it easier to keep calls on track. In A3, could we also add a short note under each objection about when it is better to suggest Basic instead of discounting Plus, so we do not overuse discounts that are meant to be exceptions?

Agree on having Plus as the default close. Maybe in A2 we can phrase it as: based on what you shared, Plus is usually the best fit, and then briefly contrast it with Basic and Premium. That keeps the decision simple for the customer.

Thanks for adding the price first branch. That is a situation I see a lot. In A7, could we also include a quick reminder to have A3 open during the call? I sometimes forget where to find the objection responses when I am in a hurry.

I have now added comments in A2 where we need to avoid promising anything beyond what is in A5, especially around refunds and cancellation timing. With those tweaks, I am comfortable saying the script and cheat sheet are consistent with our membership policies and the tier definitions in A1.

I have incorporated all the feedback: shortened discovery, added the price first branch, clarified the Plus default close, and expanded A3 with the tier confusion objection and guidance on when to move to Basic instead of discounting. A7 now includes checks for A3, A5, and tagging in A4. From my side, A2, A3, and A7 are ready for launch unless anyone spots a blocker.

I just re read A2 and A3. The flow is clear and the objections cover what I usually hear on calls. I do not see any blockers. I am comfortable using this as the standard script and cheat sheet for the pilot in T9.

Same here. A2 and A3 look solid and practical. The checklist in A7 should also help keep us consistent. I suggest we lock these for launch and only adjust after we have data from the first T9 pilot calls.
I am ok with using A2 and A3 as they are now. The examples and the clear steps in A7 make it easier for me to follow the structure during calls.

Given the feedback and the checks against A1 and A5, I agree we can lock A2 as the standard pitch script and A3 as the approved objection list for launch. Any future changes can be done after we review the pilot results from T9.

threads.thread_goal: Define target segments, outreach cadence, and prospect list priorities.

messages.text: Starting the targeting and outreach workstream. For T4, I drafted three initial customer segments and started listing accounts in the Membership Performance Tracking Sheet A4 with simple tags. For T5, I also put a first pass of an outreach cadence in the Membership Outreach Cadence and Channel Mix guideline A6, covering calls, email, and digital touchpoints for the first three weeks. Please review the segments and the cadence so we can agree on priorities.

I checked A6. The three week cadence looks reasonable, but I wonder if we should front load more calls in week one to get faster feedback for T9. On segments in A4, I like the split by engagement level, but maybe we should also tag by potential tier fit, like likely Basic, Plus, or Premium, so we can see how each tier performs.

From what I see in A4, the three segments you proposed make sense. I would suggest we prioritize the mid and high engagement groups for the first three weeks, since they are more likely to convert and give us useful feedback. For the cadence in A6, could we add a simple rule on how many attempts we make before pausing outreach on a prospect?

I saw the prospect list in A4. Some of the accounts are ones I already talk to. Should I start adding notes about which tier I think fits them best, or do we want to wait until we finalize the outreach cadence in A6?

From a membership perspective, focusing on existing engaged customers first will help us validate the tiers from A1 faster. Just a reminder that any outreach messaging should stay aligned with A2 and A5, especially around benefits and terms. Once we agree on the priority segments and cadence, I can sync with marketing so T11 stays consistent.

Good idea on front loading calls. I will adjust A6 so week one has more call attempts and fewer emails, then we rebalance in weeks two and three. I will also add a tier fit tag in A4 so we can see which prospects we are aiming for Basic, Plus, or Premium before we start T9.

I will add a simple rule in A6: up to three call attempts and two emails over the three week period before we pause a prospect, unless they explicitly ask us to stop earlier. That should keep the cadence structured without being too aggressive.

On segment priorities, I agree we should focus on mid and high engagement accounts first. For the first three weeks, I would propose we treat low engagement as a secondary segment, mainly via email, while we spend most call time on the other two groups.

That split works for me. It will also help us see in A4 how conversion differs by engagement level. Maybe we can mark in A6 that low engagement accounts get fewer total touchpoints so we do not overload the team.

Please go ahead and start adding your tier fit suggestions in A4. That will help us refine the segments and see if our assumptions match what you hear on calls. Just use the new tier fit tag column I added.
Got it, I will start tagging my accounts in A4 with the tier I think fits them best. If I am unsure, I will leave a short note so we can review together later.

Once we finalize which segments we prioritize for the first three weeks, I will update A5 with any specific eligibility notes that apply to those groups, so we do not accidentally offer a tier to a customer type that should not receive it.

To make it concrete, I propose we set the priority for the first three weeks as: 1) high engagement existing customers, 2) mid engagement existing customers, 3) selected new prospects that look like strong Plus or Premium fits, and 4) low engagement accounts mainly via email. That should give us a good mix for T9 while keeping the team focused.

I support that priority order. It matches where we are most likely to see early wins and useful feedback. With the updated A6 cadence and the tagging in A4, we should be able to track results by segment and tier.

I have updated A6 to reflect that priority order and the call heavy first week. The cadence now specifies the number of calls and emails per segment and the pause rule we discussed. Unless there are objections, I suggest we treat this outreach cadence and channel mix as final for launch.

Looks good to me. The updated A6 cadence is clear and workable, and with the tagging in A4 we will be able to see quickly which segments respond best. I am fine calling this our approved outreach plan for the first three weeks.
The cadence in A6 is clear enough for me to follow. I will focus my calls on the high and mid engagement accounts assigned to me in A4 and use email for the lower engagement ones as described.

Great, I will reflect the agreed segment priorities and outreach cadence in A5 and share a short note with marketing so they can align any external messaging. This will also help when we review T9 results and prepare any adjustments in T10.

threads.thread_goal: Run pilot, capture feedback, and refine tiers and messaging.

messages.text: Quick update on the pilot for T9: we have completed the first batch of ten membership calls using the script in A2, the objection cheat sheet A3, and the outreach plan from A6. All outcomes are logged in the Membership Performance Tracking Sheet A4, including which tier we pitched and the final result. Let us use this thread to capture key learnings and decide what, if anything, we should adjust in A1, A2, or A3.

Looking at A4, it seems Plus is getting the most interest, which matches our expectations. One pattern I noticed on calls is that some customers felt Basic was too limited once we explained it, but they were not ready for Premium either. The way we describe Basic in A2 might be making it sound weaker than it needs to be.

On my calls, I had a couple of customers ask if they could try Plus for a short period and then decide whether to stay or downgrade. I was not fully sure how to answer beyond what is in A3, so I stuck to the standard explanation. Maybe we need a clearer example in A2 or A5 for that situation.

From the notes in A4, objections about price and confusion between Plus and Premium were the most frequent. The responses in A3 worked, but in a few cases it felt like we needed a stronger value explanation for Premium, especially for heavy users. Maybe we can tweak the Premium positioning in A2 to highlight concrete outcomes more clearly.

Thanks for logging everything in A4. From a membership standpoint, I want to be careful not to change the actual benefits in A1 too quickly, but we can definitely refine how we describe them in A2 and A3. For the trial Plus then downgrade question, we need to stay within the rules in A5, so I will double check what is allowed and propose a clear answer.

Agree on Basic. In A2 we currently frame it mostly as a fallback option, which might be making it sound like a poor choice. We could rephrase it to focus on who it is right for, like budget conscious customers who still want access to core services, without underselling it.

Yes, that would help. Also, maybe in A3 we can add a short response for when someone says they only want the cheapest option, guiding them to Basic but still reminding them what they would miss compared to Plus.

For Premium, I would suggest we add one or two concrete examples in A2, like how the higher support level or exclusive perks helped similar customers. That might make the price difference easier to justify when we handle objections in A3.
If we add that example about trying Plus then downgrading, could we also include a simple sentence I can use on calls, so I do not accidentally promise something outside A5?

I checked A5 and we can allow customers to start on Plus and then move to Basic at the end of the term, but not mid term without following the standard change rules. I will add a clear example and a suggested sentence in A2 and A5 so you can explain it safely without over committing.

I will update A2 to strengthen the Premium value story with concrete outcomes and adjust the Basic description so it sounds like a valid choice for the right profile, not just a fallback. I will also add the new objection response in A3 for price sensitive customers who still want to understand the differences.
Once those changes are in A2 and A3, I think we can keep the three tier structure in A1 as is. The feedback from A4 suggests the tiers themselves are working; it is more about how we present them.

I agree. The conversion rates in A4 are promising for Plus and acceptable for Premium given the small sample. I would not change the actual benefits in A1 yet. Let us first see how the updated messaging performs in the next batch of calls.
Once you update A2 and A3, could you highlight the new parts or leave a short note in the doc? That will help me focus on what changed before my next calls.

I have now updated A2 and A3 with the new Basic and Premium wording, the extra examples, and the additional objection response. I also added comments pointing to the changed sections. No changes were made to the actual tier benefits in A1.

From my side, I confirm that the updates in A2 and A3 stay within the policy boundaries in A5 and do not change the underlying tier structure in A1. For now, I suggest we keep the tiers and pricing as they are and only adjust messaging as you have done.
Aligned. The pilot from T9 shows the structure in A1 is sound, and the refinements in A2 and A3 should address the main issues we saw. We can revisit after the next round of calls if needed.
I will keep logging the next pilot calls in A4 using the updated script and objections. That will give us a clear before and after view for the messaging changes.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on reporting format and weekly update ritual for membership performance.

messages.text: To close the loop on tracking and reporting, I have set up the Membership Performance Tracking Sheet A4 for T8 with fields for lead, segment, tier pitched, status, revenue, and source. I also drafted a Weekly Membership Sales Summary Template A8 for T12 that pulls the key numbers and highlights. Please review both so we can agree on the weekly reporting format and update cadence.

A4 looks good. The fields cover what we need to track conversion by tier and segment. For A8, I like the structure with headline metrics, breakdown by tier, and key learnings. I would suggest we add a short section for pipeline, not just closed deals, so we can see how many prospects are in each stage.

From a rep perspective, the main question is how often we need to update A4. Daily updates might be ideal, but we need to make sure it is realistic. Maybe we can agree on a minimum update cadence and then use A8 for the weekly summary.

I like that A4 is not too complicated. For me, it would help if we have a clear rule on when to update status, for example right after each call or at the end of the day. Otherwise I might forget to log some details.

On A8, I suggest we include a small table that shows performance by segment and by tier, so we can quickly see if, for example, Premium is underperforming in a certain segment. That will make it easier to decide future adjustments in T10.

I will add a pipeline section to A8 that shows counts and conversion rates by stage, using the status field from A4. That should give us a better view of how the funnel is moving, not just the final numbers.

For the update cadence, my proposal is: reps update A4 at least once per day for any membership related activity, and we use A8 for a weekly summary posted in this channel every Friday before end of day. That should balance accuracy with workload.

Daily updates in A4 are reasonable. We can add a quick reminder in A7 so reps remember to log outcomes after calls. For the weekly A8 summary, I can take the first few weeks and then we can rotate if needed.

I am ok with daily updates in A4 as long as we keep the fields simple, which they are now. The Friday A8 summary will be useful to see how the tiers are performing without digging into the sheet every time.

If we add that reminder in A7, it will help me remember to update A4 after each call or at least by the end of the day. The weekly A8 summary will also help me see how my calls contribute to the overall results.
The proposed cadence works for me. Daily updates in A4 and a Friday A8 summary will give us enough data to spot trends quickly, especially when we compare segments and tiers.

I have updated A8 with the pipeline section and the segment by tier table, and I added a note in A7 to remind reps to update A4 after membership calls. Unless there are objections, let us confirm this as our standard weekly reporting template and update cadence.

Confirmed from my side. We will use A4 as the single source of truth for membership activity, updated daily, and A8 for the weekly Friday summary. I will prepare the first report this week so we can see how it looks in practice.
Works for me as well. The structure in A8 is clear, and the daily A4 updates are manageable. This should make our weekly check ins much more focused.
I am aligned with this plan. I will make sure to keep my entries in A4 up to date so the A8 summary reflects what is happening on my calls.
